fields.expected:
I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of my work has been building software and machine-learning systems for health and workflow problems.

Right now I work on applied machine learning at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own major parts of the ML core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system: the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts, and a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so analysts can act on the output. Before that I worked with Intelehealth on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including a Python resource-availability scoring pipeline across 32 villages and an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard.

I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and am the technical lead for ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app I built end to end in Swift/SwiftUI with Supabase, including passive sleep estimation from HealthKit and Core Motion signals. We shipped it into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users.

Ask me how we got a meeting with the president of Johns Hopkins. My cofounders and I had been building ClarityAtlas, an iOS health product I led technically, and we wanted institutional support. During Lighting of the Quads we realized President Daniels was nearby. We walked over to Garland Hall, saw him through the locked doors, and knocked until someone let us pitch. That conversation eventually turned into a formal meeting months later, and we also presented to leadership from the Hopkins Data Science and AI Institute.

I bring it up because the technical work was only part of it. I built the app end to end in Swift and SwiftUI with Supabase, including a passive sleep-estimation system using HealthKit and Core Motion signals so users would not need a wearable. But shipping it into a live pilot with 30+ Hopkins users took recruiting, stakeholder conversations, and repeatedly explaining why the thing should exist. That is the part I underestimated.
